sections.heading: What makes a Jujutsu Kaisen-inspired poster distinctive?

blocks.text: Jujutsu Kaisen-inspired custom posters draw on the visual language of modern dark shonen anime: crisp linework, sharp facial angles, high-contrast shadows, dramatic perspective, and energetic effects that suggest supernatural power. A cool palette, dark clothing, and a focused expression can create the intense atmosphere fans love without turning your portrait into a copy of an existing character.

Your finished artwork is designed around you. Our artists map your real proportions—including cheekbones, eye spacing, nose bridge, hairstyle, and expression—into an original sorcerer-inspired design. Cursed-energy-style effects wrap around your character rather than covering your identity, so the result still looks recognisably like you.

sections.heading: How to turn your photo into a style-inspired poster

blocks.text: Start with a clear, well-lit photo showing the face and the features you want the artist to preserve. A phone photograph is fine for a custom anime portrait from photo, provided the face is not hidden by heavy filters, glare, sunglasses, or extreme shadows. You can submit one image or several references if you want the artist to combine a hairstyle from one photo with the expression or outfit from another.

Next, describe the feeling you want. A serious or smirking expression works well for this style, while a relaxed smile can make the finished poster more approachable. Tell us whether you prefer a close-up, waist-up design, action pose, paired composition, or group scene. You can also suggest cool or warm energy colours, a uniform-inspired outfit, a technique-like effect, or a simple background atmosphere.

items: Choose the clearest front-facing or three-quarter photo available.
Mention the desired mood: intense, mysterious, playful, heroic, or understated.
Describe pose, clothing, background, colour palette, and energy effects.
For couples or groups, identify each person and explain how you want them arranged.
Add any features that must remain accurate, such as glasses, freckles, tattoos, or a particular hairstyle.

sections.heading: What details should you provide for a commission?

blocks.text: The more useful context you provide, the easier it is for the artist to build a poster that feels intentional. You do not need to know illustration terminology. A short note such as “back-to-back, cool blue and red energy, serious expressions, dark city background” gives the artist a clear starting point. If you have no firm concept, simply share the photo and explain who the artwork is for; the artist can develop a fitting composition.

For a multi-person poster, include all reference photos together and explain the relationship between the subjects. Couples may request a back-to-back sorcerer composition, while friends or roommates might prefer a three-person team layout. Matching wallpapers, birthday gifts, and dramatic solo bedroom posters can all be adapted to the same hand-drawn approach.

Personal references are welcome, but the final design remains fan-art inspired and original. You can request a dark shonen atmosphere or familiar visual cues, but the artwork will not reproduce a named character, official costume, logo, or exact scene.

Anime Cabinet uses human artists, not AI filters or automatic photo-to-anime generators. Your reference images and notes are reviewed before the artist develops an original composition in the selected style. This gives you more control over the details that matter: likeness, pose, expression, outfit, colour balance, and the amount of supernatural atmosphere.

blocks.text: Unlimited free revisions are included, so you can ask for changes rather than settling for a first draft that does not feel right. Revision notes might include adjusting the expression, making the energy effect subtler, changing the background, refining hair volume, or bringing the likeness closer to your reference.
